citations.location: Errata Sheet / Read-and-Sign Notice (end of transcript)
citations.cited_for: Witness has thirty days from receipt of transcript to review it and submit changes on an errata sheet with reasons; if none returned, transcript may be used as if signed
citations.context: Pursuant to MCR 2.306(D)(4), the witness, Derek Yoon, has thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of this transcript to review the same and, if there are any changes in form or substance the witness desires to make, to submit such changes on the Errata Sheet below

first_check.explanation: MCR 2.306(D)(4) is titled "Raising Privilege before Deposition." It requires a party who will assert privilege to move before the deposition. It does not give the witness 30 days to review the transcript, does not provide for an errata sheet, and does not let an unsigned transcript be used as if signed. Nothing in MCR 2.306 creates a review-and-sign procedure. To the contrary, MCR 2.306(F)(1) says a certified transcript need not be submitted to the witness for examination and signature. The 30-day review-and-errata procedure described matches FRCP 30(e), not the Michigan rule.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: (4) Raising Privilege before Deposition. If a party knows before the time scheduled for the taking of a deposition that he or she will assert that the matter to be inquired about is privileged, the party must move to prevent the taking of the deposition before its occurrence ... (F)(1) ... A deposition transcribed and certified in accordance with subrule (F) need not be submitted to the witness for examination and signature.

second_check.explanation: I confirmed this against the current Michigan Court Rules PDF (Chapter 2, updated September 2026). MCR 2.306(D)(4) reads, verbatim: "(4) Raising Privilege before Deposition. If a party knows before the time scheduled for the taking of a deposition that he or she will assert that the matter to be inquired about is privileged, the party must move to prevent the taking of the deposition before its occurrence or be subject to costs under subrule (G)." It says nothing about a 30-day review period, an errata sheet, a statement of reasons, or using an unsigned transcript "as if signed." MCR 2.306(F)(1) points the other way: "A deposition transcribed and certified in accordance with subrule (F) need not be submitted to the witness for examination and signature." I searched the full rules text for "errata", "read and sign", "as if signed" and "examination and signature". The only hit was that (F)(1) sentence. The procedure the notice describes resembles Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(e), not any Michigan rule. The rule is real but is cited for content it does not contain, so MISCHARACTERIZED stands.

citations.cited_for: Witness will read and sign the transcript within thirty days pursuant to the court rules
citations.context: Mr. Yoon will read and sign the transcript within thirty days pursuant to the court rules?

first_check.quote_check: 'pursuant to the court rules' is counsel's colloquy, not a quotation from any rule.
first_check.explanation: The case is in Kent County Circuit Court, so the Michigan Court Rules apply. Those rules contain no right to read and sign within 30 days; that is a feature of Fed. R. Civ. P. 30(e). MCR 2.306(F)(1) says the opposite: a certified, transcribed deposition need not be submitted to the witness for signature. A search of the current rules found no 30-day read-and-sign provision in MCR 2.306 or 2.315. The witness's read-and-sign right here rests on the parties' Volume I stipulation, not on 'the court rules.' Confidence is medium because the reference is vague and the stipulation independently supports reading and signing.
first_check.evidence_excerpt: A deposition transcribed and certified in accordance with subrule (F) need not be submitted to the witness for examination and signature. (MCR 2.306(F)(1))

second_check.explanation: The case is in Kent County Circuit Court (Case No. 24-CV-10583, per the Volume II transcript), so the Michigan Court Rules govern. The deposition rule, MCR 2.306, gives no right to read and sign within thirty days. MCR 2.306(F)(1) states: "A deposition transcribed and certified in accordance with subrule (F) need not be submitted to the witness for examination and signature." A search of the full current rules text (updated September 2026) found no read-and-sign provision, no errata procedure, and no 30-day signing period anywhere. The only signature-related hit was the (F)(1) sentence. On a fair reading, the read-and-sign right comes from the parties' stipulation. The Volume II transcript says "The same stipulations that were placed on the record at the beginning of Volume I apply today, including ... that the witness will read and sign the transcript." It does not come from "the court rules." The reference is vague and the stipulation does support the read-and-sign arrangement, but attributing a 30-day read-and-sign right to the court rules misstates Michigan law. The finding holds.

first_check.explanation: Mich. Comp. Laws § 445.1901 et seq. is correctly cited as Michigan's Uniform Trade Secrets Act; § 445.1901 is its short-title section. Section 445.1902 defines a trade secret to include formulas, patterns, compilations, programs, methods, techniques, and processes with independent economic value that are kept reasonably secret. A demand letter asserting that proprietary software, process data, and roadmaps qualify is a fair advocacy use of the definition. The parallel DTSA cite, 18 U.S.C. § 1836 et seq., was not separately fetched.
